target_customer: Quantitative trading firms running parallel simulations and backtests, then AI teams running RL, fine-tuning and batch inference
problem: Large parallel workloads need cheap, huge CPU and GPU clusters across hyperscalers and neoclouds. Zibra builds distributed clusters from the cheapest capacity with low scheduling overhead.
business_model: Usage-based compute orchestration on spot capacity
product_category: AI and HPC infrastructure, distributed compute runtime

founders.name: Zac Policzer
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a career in large database software serving over a billion people; company site says founders built LinkedIn's Venice, Liquid and Espresso.

competitors.name: CoreWeave
competitors.what: Purpose-built AI cloud pitched at quant researchers with GPU-heavy parallel workloads

technical_complexity.rationale: Scheduling millions of parallel tasks across multiple clouds on spot capacity with under 50 ms dispatch overhead requires deep distributed systems skill, which the founders have from Ray and LinkedIn.

defensibility.rationale: Hard distributed systems know-how and Ray lineage, but compute resale layers are commoditized and customers can switch.

market_need_then: Quant firms run large backtests and AI labs need cheap parallel compute; Zibra claims clusters of 100 to 50,000 nodes with up to 6.4 million parallel tasks (company claims).

branding.domain_note: Uses zibralabs.ai; Labs suffix, since the exact name is shared with an unrelated Ukrainian company Zibra AI.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, concise and metric-driven with the line Frontier-grade AI Infrastructure for Everyone

brand_strength.rationale: Name is confusable with Zibra AI and a zebra-themed design brand; credibility rests on founder pedigree, not brand.

outcome_analysis: Zibra Labs joined YC in Spring 2026 with two founders who include a former Ray tech lead. No outcome yet. It starts with quant trading backtesting as a wedge and plans to extend to AI workloads, with competition from neoclouds and compute platforms.
notes: Aggregators report about $500K, labeled seed (PitchBook, with Founder Factor, HOF Capital, Team Ignite Ventures and YC) or pre-seed (VCBacked), dated January or May 2026; no primary source, so not recorded as a round. Competitor search returned only undated vendor posts, so only CoreWeave is listed with a null date. Outcome search found nothing about Zibra Labs. Completeness pass: Round recorded from PitchBook (seed, July 2026) and VCBacked (pre-seed, May 2026): both give about $500K, stage and date conflict so stage other and date null. Single database family, no press source; HOF Capital seen only in PitchBook.
